# geta

> geta is a Go (1.27+) framework for typed HTTP JSON APIs, built on the standard library alone. An operation is a typed Go function; its input and output types, with `schema` tags, are the contract: geta binds and validates every request against them, answers refusals as RFC 9457 problems, and derives the OpenAPI 3.1 document from the same types. geta is strict: it refuses rather than coerces, and `geta.New` refuses a misdeclared application at startup, listing every mistake.

Read this file first; it is enough to write a working application. Routes are written as a table, as below, or as a directory tree that `geta sync` turns into one ([Starting an application](docs/guide/start.md)). Each section of the guide covers one subject in full, for when a detail matters.

## A whole application

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/koji-1009/geta"
)

// The request body. Every member is required unless it is a pointer tagged omitzero.
type NewItem struct {
	Name string   `json:"name" schema:"minLength=1,maxLength=100"`
	Kind string   `json:"kind" schema:"enum=book|tool"`
	Due  *string  `json:"due,omitzero" schema:"format=date"`
	Tags []string `json:"tags" schema:"maxItems=10,items.minLength=1,items.maxLength=30"`
}

type Item struct {
	ID      string `json:"id"`
	NewItem        // untagged embedded struct: its members are Item's
}

// Inputs: one tag per field (path, query, header, cookie, or body).
type ItemPath struct {
	ID string `path:"id" schema:"maxLength=64"`
}
type CreateIn struct {
	Body NewItem `body:"json"`
}
type ListIn struct {
	Kind  *string `query:"kind" schema:"enum=book|tool"`                    // pointer: optional
	Limit int     `query:"limit" schema:"minimum=1,maximum=100,default=20"` // default: optional
}
type PutIn struct {
	geta.RequireConditional // binds If-Match; 428 without it
	ItemPath
	Body NewItem `body:"json"`
}

// Outputs: a plain struct is the JSON body; a struct with header/body tags is an envelope.
type List struct {
	Items []Item `json:"items"`
}
type Created struct {
	Location string `header:"Location"`
	Body     Item   `body:"json"`
}
type Tagged struct {
	ETag string `header:"ETag"`
	Body Item   `body:"json"`
}

var errNotFound = errors.New("no such item")

type store struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	items   map[string]Item
	version map[string]int
	n       int
}

func etag(v int) string { return `"v` + strconv.Itoa(v) + `"` }

func Table() geta.Table {
	s := &store{items: map[string]Item{}, version: map[string]int{}}
	// Failure rows map errors the handlers return to statuses.
	notFound := []geta.Failure{geta.On(errNotFound, http.StatusNotFound, "no such item")}
	return geta.Table{Routes: []geta.Entry{
		{Path: "/items", Route: geta.Route{
			Get: geta.Op(http.StatusOK, func(ctx context.Context, in *ListIn) (*List, error) {
				return &List{Items: []Item{}}, nil
			}, geta.Doc{Summary: "List items"}),
			Post: geta.Op(http.StatusCreated, func(ctx context.Context, in *CreateIn) (*Created, error) {
				s.mu.Lock()
				defer s.mu.Unlock()
				s.n++
				it := Item{ID: strconv.Itoa(s.n), NewItem: in.Body}
				s.items[it.ID], s.version[it.ID] = it, 1
				return &Created{Location: "/items/" + it.ID, Body: it}, nil
			}, geta.Doc{Summary: "Create an item"}),
		}},
		{Path: "/items/{id}", Route: geta.Route{
			Get: geta.Op(http.StatusOK, func(ctx context.Context, in *ItemPath) (*Tagged, error) {
				s.mu.Lock()
				defer s.mu.Unlock()
				it, ok := s.items[in.ID]
				if !ok {
					return nil, errNotFound
				}
				return &Tagged{ETag: etag(s.version[in.ID]), Body: it}, nil
			}, geta.Doc{Failures: notFound}),
			Put: geta.Op(http.StatusOK, func(ctx context.Context, in *PutIn) (*Tagged, error) {
				s.mu.Lock()
				defer s.mu.Unlock()
				if _, ok := s.items[in.ID]; !ok {
					return nil, errNotFound
				}
				// 412 when If-Match is not the current tag; return the error as is.
				if err := in.Check(etag(s.version[in.ID]), time.Time{}); err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}
				s.version[in.ID]++
				it := Item{ID: in.ID, NewItem: in.Body}
				s.items[in.ID] = it
				return &Tagged{ETag: etag(s.version[in.ID]), Body: it}, nil
			}, geta.Doc{Failures: notFound}),
			Delete: geta.OpNoBody(http.StatusNoContent, func(ctx context.Context, in *ItemPath) error {
				s.mu.Lock()
				defer s.mu.Unlock()
				if _, ok := s.items[in.ID]; !ok {
					return errNotFound
				}
				delete(s.items, in.ID)
				return nil
			}, geta.Doc{Failures: notFound}),
		}},
	}}
}

func main() {
	a, err := geta.New(Table())
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err) // every assembly mistake, all at once
	}
	log.Fatal(geta.Run(context.Background(), &http.Server{Addr: ":8080", Handler: a}))
}
```

Test it in process with getatest; every response is checked against the document:

```go
func TestItems(t *testing.T) {
	c := getatest.New(t, Table()) // runs geta.New: an assembly mistake fails here
	if res := c.Post("/items", map[string]any{"name": "Go", "kind": "book", "tags": []string{}}); res.Status != 201 {
		t.Fatal(res.Status, res.Text())
	}
	p := c.Post("/items", map[string]any{"name": "", "kind": "pen", "tags": []string{}, "x": 1}).Problem()
	// p.Errors: $.name (minLength), $.kind (enum), $.x (unknown member), all listed in one 400
	_ = p
}
```

What geta answers on its own, with no code: 400 listing every violation, unknown members included (`errors`: `{"in":"body","path":"$.name","message":"…"}`; a parameter's path is its name, `limit`), 404 and 405 (with `Allow`), 415 for a body that is not `application/json`, 428 and 412 for `RequireConditional`, 500 for an error no failure row matches, all as `application/problem+json`. `a.OpenAPI()` is the document as JSON bytes; geta does not serve it, so mount `a` and a handler for it on an `http.ServeMux` of your own if it should be served.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- A JSON member is required unless it is a pointer tagged `json:"name,omitzero"`; `omitempty` and every other json option are refused. Slice elements are never pointers (`[]T`, not `[]*T`). `null` is accepted only in `geta.Nullable[T]`. `any` and `map[string]any` have no JSON form.
- Schema keywords: `minLength maxLength pattern format enum minimum maximum exclusiveMinimum exclusiveMaximum multipleOf minItems maxItems uniqueItems`; `items.` applies one to slice elements; `default=` makes a field optional. Lengths count characters. A `pattern` refuses `.`, `\s`, `\S` (write a set: `[^\n]`, `[ \t]`).
- `format=` names only `date date-time time duration ipv4 ipv6 uuid` (and json-pointer, relative-json-pointer, password), each checked (`2026-02-30` is 400); there is no `email`: use a `pattern` or your own text type ([Format types](docs/guide/formats.md)). The same formats exist as types (`geta.Date`, `geta.DateTime`, `geta.Duration`, `geta.IPv4`, …).
- Handlers return the lower layer's errors unchanged; `Doc.Failures` maps them (`geta.On(sentinel, status, detail)`, `geta.OnAs[*MyErr](status, detail)`). An error no row matches is a logged 500; `err.Error()` never reaches the client.
- A 201 with `Location`, a redirect, an `ETag`, or several success statuses need an output envelope (fields tagged `header:"…"`, `body:"json"`, `status:"200|201"`).
- Embed `geta.Conditional` (or `geta.RequireConditional`, which answers 428 when no precondition is sent) to bind If-Match and the other precondition headers; call `in.Check(etag, modified)` before acting and return its error as is (a 304 or 412).
- Named struct types are components named after the type, so `users.Path` and `items.Path` in two route packages fail `geta.New`; give route-local types unique names.

Not in geta: DI containers, string route registration, HTTP error types, static files, sessions, templates, rate limiting, doc UI, security headers (set them in a root middleware of your own; geta sets only `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`). A cookie-session app's CSRF, proxy client address, and idempotency keys: see `examples/bookmarks`.

- [Starting an application](docs/guide/start.md): a route tree, file by file, with `geta sync` and the generated test
- [The route tree](docs/guide/tree.md): directories as URLs, matching, OPTIONS, writing the table by hand
- [Routes, operations, and input](docs/guide/operations.md): the canonical route, operations, deprecation, parameters, deepObject
- [JSON bodies, null, and components](docs/guide/json.md): required and optional members, maps, time.Time, geta.Nullable, nil slices on output, component names
- [Constraints and limits](docs/guide/schema.md): every `schema` keyword, element and key keywords, backstops, violation lists
- [Form, multipart, and raw bodies](docs/guide/bodies.md): and Content-Type and Content-Encoding of a request
- [Format types](docs/guide/formats.md): date, date-time, time, duration, ipv4, ipv6, uuid, and formats your application decides
- [Sealed types](docs/guide/sealed.md): oneOf with a discriminator
- [Output envelopes](docs/guide/outputs.md): headers, cookies, several statuses, redirects
- [Conditional requests](docs/guide/conditional.md): ETag, If-Match, 304, 412, 428
- [Errors](docs/guide/errors.md): failure rows, problems, problems that carry the error's data
- [Scopes and middleware](docs/guide/middleware.md): order, timeouts, CORS, compression, ETag, where your own rate limiter goes
- [Security](docs/guide/security.md): the gate, schemes, cookie sessions, JWT
- [Streams and upgrades](docs/guide/streams.md): server-sent events, WebSocket
- [Assembly, serving, and the document](docs/guide/serving.md): `geta.Run`, the OpenAPI document, HTTP/3
- [Testing](docs/guide/testing.md): getatest, golden documents
- [The geta command and getavet](docs/guide/tools.md)
